sources.excerpt: Red Llama 3.0 - **Builder:** Way Huge - **Catalog type:** Overdrive - **Identity:** Way Huge Smalls Red Llama, model WM23, the compact anniversary-era return of the Red Llama family. The WM23 Smalls Red Llama is the compact return of the Red Llama Overdrive. Jim Dunlop identifies the original RL2 as Way Huge's first production pedal, introduced in 1992, and describes the WM23 as a smaller-format return intended to reproduce the harmonic, touch-sensitive character of the earlier Red Llama. - Way Huge Smalls enclosure with Red Llama graphics. - Finish/artwork differences remain variations unless the underlying product is materially different. - First Way Huge production pedal, introduced in **1992**. - Harmonic overdrive with a crunchy tweed-style character. - **1,000 pieces worldwide**. - Smaller pedalboard-friendly housing. - Added **Hi-Cut** control. - Compact anniversary-era version. - Controls: **Volume** and **Drive**. - Hardwire-relay bypass. - 9V battery or compatible external supply. - RL2 established the 1992 original. - WHE-206 added Hi-Cut and limited-edition 25th-anniversary treatment. - WM23 brought the Red Llama back in the smaller Smalls enclosure with the two-knob external control layout. - Exact production transistor/device information is not specified in the manufacturer documentation reviewed. - Exact production clipping/rectification diode information is not specified in the manufacturer documentation reviewed. Way Huge describes the Red Llama as a harmonic overdrive capable of moving from soft, touch-sensitive drive into more aggressive, fuzz-like saturation. The WM23 is intended to retain the warm, crunchy tweed-like character of the original in a compact enclosure. 1. Download this manual POWER The Red Llama™ Overdrive is powered by a single 9-volt battery, a 9-volt AC adapter such as the Dunlop ECB003, or the DC Brick and Iso-Brick power supplies. The power input is a 5.5mm x 2.1mm ™ jack with the positive voltage on the outer sleeve. Using an external power supply will disconnect the battery. Disconnect the input jack to preserve battery life when not in use. The pedal will lock into bypass mode when it is time to change the battery. It also includes power protection circuitr y to prevent damage from AC power supplies.
